description: yavs (Yet Another VHDL Simulator): a VHDL-1993/2008/2019 simulator written in Rust with a command line interface (analyze, elab, run), compiled-code tiers, coverage, FST waveforms, DAP debugging and a VHPI plugin interface.
rules: yavs is a command line tool: analyze VHDL into a library with `yavs analyze --std=2008 --work=NAME:PATH files...`, then simulate with `yavs run --work=NAME:PATH TOP`. `yavs elab` only checks that a design elaborates.
Write options in the `--name=value` form (for example `--work=lib:out/lib`, `--stop-time=10ms`); generics are `-gNAME=VALUE`, one argument each.
Each file is parsed with its own standard (`--std=93`, `2008` or `2019`), so files of different standards can share one project.

The compiled tier depends on the build: a build without features is interpreter only (`--tier=auto` and `--tier=clift` are then error E0120); release archives (Cranelift) and source builds with `--features clift` default to `--tier=auto`, which compiles hot functions in the background. A tier the build lacks is error E0120. The output is identical on every tier; `--tier=interp` is the simplest to debug, and a `--dap` debugger session always runs the interpreter.

Keep the `yavs-cache/` directory beside the library between runs: the second run of a design stores the analysis and compiled code, later runs and the other test cases of a testbench reuse it. `--no-cache` turns it off.
`--threads N` (default 1) spreads process evaluation over N threads with byte-identical output; it only pays off in designs with many processes waking in the same delta cycle.

Coverage workflow: run each test with `yavs run --cov=NAME.ycov --cov-kind=statement,branch,toggle,condition`, then merge and report with `yavs cov report all.ycov --html DIR --cobertura FILE`. Write `--cov=FILE`, not `--cov FILE`.
Record waveforms with `--wave=FILE.fst` (FST format, readable by common waveform viewers); limit them with `--wave-exclude` globs on large designs.
Errors and warnings carry stable codes such as E1100; `yavs --explain CODE` prints the explanation. A failed step stops the run: nothing runs after a failed analyze.
Check `docs/language-support.md` before relying on a VHDL-2019 or PSL feature: PSL is a subset. VHPI support is partial, see `docs/vhpi.md`.

Start with the Getting started page (a testbench in `docs/examples`: analyze, run, `-gEXPECTED=5` for a failing run, exit statuses 0 and 1). The Command-line reference page lists the user-facing options; `yavs --explain CODE` and the Errors and troubleshooting page explain diagnostics. Debugging: `yavs run --dap` for VS Code (extension in `editors/vscode`) and other Debug Adapter Protocol clients; VHPI plugins load with `--vhpi`.
